who_for: The right grill depends on how you like to cook. Gas grills heat up fast and suit weeknight dinners. Charcoal and kamado grills give more smoky flavor and higher searing heat. Pellet grills make low-and-slow smoking easy.
If you cook for a crowd, look at the main cooking area. If you camp or tailgate, a portable model makes more sense than a big cart grill.

how_we_picked.label: Even heat
how_we_picked.text: Consistent heat across the cooking surface, without big hot and cold spots, was our first priority.

how_we_picked.label: Build quality
how_we_picked.text: We favored sturdy materials like porcelain-enameled cast iron grates and stainless steel burners that hold up for years outdoors.

how_we_picked.label: Temperature control
how_we_picked.text: For pellet and kamado grills, we looked at how well they hold a set temperature during long cooks.

how_we_picked.label: Size and features
how_we_picked.text: We compared cooking area to typical family needs and weighed extras like side burners and Wi-Fi temperature monitoring.

how_we_picked.label: Warranty
how_we_picked.text: Long warranties on burners and fireboxes are a good sign a grill is built to last.
